lit.\u0027\u003cp class=\"muted small\"\u003:
"

Compare the rate constants at two temperatures: ln(k₂/k₁) = (Ea/R)·(1/T₁ − 1/T₂).

"

"

With Ea = 53 kJ/mol the rate doubles on going from 298 K to 308 K. For smaller Ea the effect of temperature is weaker; for larger Ea, stronger.

"

"

Activation energies and rates are scaled so that the reactions can be seen in seconds (real molecular Ea are larger and the effective fraction much smaller). The qualitative relationships and the equations are the real ones.

"

"

A straight line of slope −Ea/R: the larger the Ea, the “steeper” the dependence of k on temperature. The dot marks the current T.

lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAl acercarse, las nub:
"

As they approach, the electron clouds repel each other and the energy increases. The B–C bond weakens (order < 1) while A–B begins to form. Observe in the graph that the point climbs the barrier.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eAl subir T aumenta la:
"

As T rises the collision frequency increases and, above all, so does the fraction of molecules with E ≥ Ea: the curve broadens and shifts. The Arrhenius equation summarizes it: k = A·e−Ea/RT.

In real reactions with Ea ≈ 50–60 kJ/mol, +10 K near 298 K roughly doubles the rate.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eCada partícula tiene:
"

Each particle has a reactive zone (the light patch). Only if the patches face each other can the collision be effective. This is summarized in the steric factor p.

As p decreases more orange collisions appear: there is energy to spare, but the geometry is not right.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl catalizador no cam:
"

The catalyst does not change ΔH or the composition at equilibrium: it lowers the barrier (here to 55 %). More collisions manage to overcome it and the catalyst is recovered unconsumed.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEl enlace A–B termina:
"

The A–B bond finishes forming and B–C breaks: the system “falls” down the other side of the barrier and the energy drops to that of the products ("
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eEn el máximo del cami:
"

At the maximum of the lowest-energy path the A···B and B···C bonds are partial (orders close to 0.5). This activated complex is not an isolable substance: it lasts ≈ 10⁻¹³ s, the time of one vibration. Its energy relative to the reactants is the Ea ("
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLa energía cinética r:
"

The relative kinetic energy must exceed the activation energy Ea. As Ea increases (the line in the graph shifts to the right) the area of molecules with E ≥ Ea decreases and the reaction becomes slower.

Approximately, that fraction is e−Ea/RT.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eLas moléculas se muev:
"

The molecules move in all directions and collide ceaselessly. Not all move equally fast: their energies follow the Maxwell–Boltzmann distribution (Energy tab).

There is no reaction yet: observe the A (red) and B (blue) particles.

"
lit.\u0027\u003cp\u003eSegún la \u003cb\u003:
"

According to collision theory, A and B must collide to react; but only a small fraction of collisions is effective.

The flash indicates the outcome: gray = insufficient energy, orange = poor orientation, green = effective collision (AB forms, purple).

"
